correctness.rationale: The 2025 same-object Theorem 5.10 rigorously supplies homology in degree 2 only and rank 6k^2-1 for all k>=2. For each nonzero translation, the coordinate orbit-diameter estimate excludes every fixed simplex unless it is one of four axial order-three shifts; in those cases exactly 3k^2 triangles are invariant with positive orientation. The signed simplicial Lefschetz theorem yields the exact character. The sum of two coset permutation characters minus the trivial character matches it pointwise; rational semisimplicity proves module equality. A standalone verifier independently enumerates all oriented fixed simplices for k=2,3 and checks a complete acyclic Morse matching proving the already-known k=2 homotopy type. No finite-experiment extrapolation or integer splitting is asserted.

value.rationale: The module formula distinguishes the full translation symmetry of infinitely many canonical critical torus-grid Rips complexes even though their nonequivariant homotopy types were completely known. It identifies two natural coordinate directions, all exceptional axial order-three character values, every Fourier multiplicity, and a one-dimensional invariant summand. None of these invariants follow from the published Betti number or sphere-wedge count without new fixed-simplex arguments. Such group-action information is useful for equivariant topology, quotient homology and symmetry-aware persistence.
